quotes.text: There are fifty options here and I just froze, I can't decide.
Only three choices, easy, I picked straight away.
The blue one caught my eye, that's the one I remember.
I expected it to work like my email app, and it does.
I assumed swipe would go back like on my phone, and it didn't.
It rejected my phone number because I put spaces in it.
I typed the date any old way and it understood.
I never read the tour, I just skipped it and started clicking.
That one moment when it found my file instantly, that's what I'll remember.
It all went fine and then the last screen crashed, so the whole thing feels bad.
That half-finished form is nagging at me, I want to go back and complete it.
I'm on step 4 of 5, I'm not stopping now.
By the time I got to the last option I'd forgotten the first one.
It looks so polished I just assumed it would work.
It's a bit clunky but it's so pretty I don't mind.
I thought those two buttons went together because they were next to each other.
The related settings are boxed together, it's obvious what belongs to what.
I thought that big banner was an ad so I never looked at it.
It makes me pick the region, the format, the codec — why can't it just do it?
It just worked it out for me, I didn't have to choose anything.
The buttons are tiny and right next to each other, I keep hitting the wrong one.
There's too much to take in on this screen, I can't process it.
It responds instantly, it feels like it's keeping up with me.
Every click takes two seconds and it's driving me mad.
I just went with whatever was pre-selected, I didn't look at the others.
quotes.note: Thaler retired; Nielsen remembered for me / risky default

quotes.text: I usually explore a new city on foot the first day, no map.
